messages:
alex: Heads-up — got a billing alert: compute spend spiked 4.2x in the last 3 hours. Punching the graphs now :eyes:
infra-bot: [ALERT] cloud-billing@redwood — daily compute cost anomaly detected (delta +320% vs rolling 7d). Invoice link: https://billing.cloudprovider.example/org/12345/charges/2026-03-18
priya: link? can you paste the top line items.
alex: https://billing.cloudprovider.example/summary/2026-03-18
alex: top line items: p4d.24xlarge on-demand usage = 1288 instance-hours, spot GPU pools show zero — cost contribution ~ $190k
rick: whoa. we don't run p4d in prod normally. Autoscaler should prefer cheaper families (a10g/g5) and spot.
sasha: did anything change with the autoscaler or terraform exposure variables last night? I merged a small change to nodepool priorities in #infra-terraform
priya: tagging @sasha @rick — can you grep the autoscaler logs for "fallback_to_on_demand"?
rick: running now from control-plane
rick: ```
$ kubectl logs -n kube-system cluster-autoscaler-xyz | tail -n 200
I0307 02:45:12 autoscaler.go:123] Pod xyz pending (needs gpu): looking for nodegroup
I0307 02:45:12 scale.go:87] Launching instance in nodegroup gpu-spot-1 (capacity 40) using launch-template gpu-spot-template
E0307 02:45:30 scale.go:145] Spot capacity exhausted in region us-west-2; falling back to on-demand
I0307 02:45:31 scale.go:147] Selected instance type p4d.24xlarge based on fallback priority list
I0307 02:45:31 scale.go:150] Requested 250 instances -> launching 250 on-demand p4d
```
rick: that log is from 02:45 UTC, matches billing spike window.
alex: 250 on-demand p4d instances for ~5 hours explains the $190k
sasha: ugh — my terraform change reordered the variable gpu_priority_list to prefer p4d first as a temporary test for perf evals, I thought it was gated behind a feature flag but looks like the var default was changed in the live module.
priya: can you paste the terraform diff? we need to confirm exact commit
sasha: ```
- gpu_priority_list = ["g5", "a10g", "p4d"]
+ gpu_priority_list = ["p4d", "g5", "a10g"]
```
sasha: I removed the gating when resolving a merge conflict. I thought only internal test clusters used that module — not prod. huge mistake.
alex: ok stop new launches: scale down policy now -> set max nodes to current count so autoscaler stops creating more, and add scale-in protection removal for the p4d pool
rick: doing the kube-side throttles now
bill: @alex @priya we'll also need to notify finance and open a cloud provider support case for credits; this looks like an accidental launch due to config, not sustained usage
priya: finance pinged. I'm patching terraform to revert gpu_priority_list and will push a hotfix to prevent reordering without flag.
sasha: pushing revert now and adding a guard in the module variable validation.
sasha: ```hcl
variable "gpu_priority_list" {
  type = list(string)
  validation {
    condition     = contains(var.feature_flags, "allow_gpu_reorder")
    error_message = "gpu_priority_list can only be changed when allow_gpu_reorder is enabled"
  }
}
```
sasha: will apply in ~5m to nodepool module
rick: I'm also running a cleanup to terminate the p4d nodegroup instances older than 20m and cordon drains where appropriate. kubectl drain script queued.
rick: ```
$ aws autoscaling set-instance-health --instance-id i-xxxx --health-status Unhealthy
$ aws autoscaling terminate-instance-in-auto-scaling-group --instance-id i-xxxx --no-should-decrement-desired-capacity
```
priya: quick ask for cost mitigation: can we convert some of this burst into reserved capacity commitments retroactively? finance?
bill: retroactive conversion not possible but we can request goodwill credits and look at convertible discounts for next quarter. Also run a pre-commitment forecast: if we keep baseline + burst risk, what RI/commitment size covers us.
alex: action items: 1) sasha revert and add validation (in progress) 2) rick terminate unwanted p4d on-demand instances (in progress) 3) priya open cloud support + billing dispute (done) 4) bill/finance to prepare committed use recommendation 5) add an alert on fallback-to-on-demand picks for GPUs (new)
sasha: applying terraform plan now
sasha: plan shows revert only, applying
sasha: apply complete. gpu_priority_list reverted and module validation added. will put a patch to gate that module change behind a feature flag in the pipeline.
rick: terminated ~210 of 250 p4d instances so far. draining nodes and rescheduling pods to a10g pools.
priya: billing case opened, case #CB-2026-3021. asked for credit due to misconfiguration
bill: finance prepping ROI analysis for reserved capacity; I'll post suggested commitment sizes by tomorrow EOD.
alex: thanks all. postmortem will live in /postmortems/ once we stabilize. short-term: add a CI check to prevent module variable reorders in prod branches.
infra-bot: [UPDATE] incident recorded: INC-2026-0320 "autoscaler fallback priority caused on-demand p4d launch (billing spike)" — responders: alex, priya, rick, sasha, bill
sasha: sorry team — will follow up with a remediation doc and checklist for editing live infra modules. :pray:
priya: no blame — let's lock this down. closing TODOs as we go.
